name: httpapi
task: A JSON API over HTTP/1.1 keep-alive with each language's std HTTP server: create, read, replace and delete items (`POST /items`, `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /items/{id}`) and list a tag's items by id (`GET /items?tag=&limit=`), the store in memory behind a reader-writer lock, every body JSON, gzip-compressed from 256 bytes when the client accepts gzip (README.md).

skip.c: no std HTTP (C's std has no sockets)
skip.rust: no std HTTP (std::net is TCP only; an HTTP server is a crate, hyper or axum over tokio, and none is in the local cargo registry, which holds serde_json and flate2: an eco cell is a fetch request to the owner, ruling Q8)

models.mk: tasks (std.http.Serve, one task per connection and one arena per request, MK_CARRIERS=8)
models.zig: OS threads (std.http.Server, one Io.Group.concurrent thread per connection)

notes: The Mk side is a new program (`mk/httpapi.mk`, D-845), written from the documents only, as an outside user, and frozen before its first publish.

The load is tools/bench's route mix (apibench.go): each connection keeps at most 12 items under its own two tags and draws from splitmix(seed + i) POST 25%, GET 30%, list 20%, PUT 13%, DELETE 10% and a POST with an out-of-range qty 2% (422); a GET, PUT or DELETE names a deleted id one time in (live items + 1), for a 404; half the requests accept gzip. Every response's status, Content-Type, Location, Content-Encoding and body are checked, the body byte for byte after gunzip.
Connections close with a reset (linger 0), as the http row's; 256 connections hold 512 sockets at once, below the owner's 10,000 cap.
